blogs.title: Pre‑operative Heparin: How a Tiny Dose Can Trigger Early Cardiac Surgery HIT
blogs.description: This post examines how even a modest, single exposure to unfractionated heparin during a pre‑procedure catheterization can ignite HIT in the first 5 days after cardiac bypass, a window typically considered too early for classic HIT. By reviewing the pathophysiology and peri‑operative practices that may predispose to this scenario, clinicians learn how to minimize hidden heparin exposure and anticipate early thrombocytopenia.

blogs.title: When the Platelet Activation Test Gives Us a Puzzle: Recognizing Autoimmune HIT with Partial Fc‑Blockade Resistance
blogs.description: The serotonin‑release assay is the cornerstone of HIT diagnosis, yet a subset of patients shows only partial inhibition by the anti‑Fc receptor monoclonal antibody IV.3. This article decodes that atypical lab signature—strong activation at zero heparin, heparin‑independent release, and incomplete Fc blockade—and explains why this points to autoimmune HIT rather than classic, heparin‑dependent HIT.

blogs.title: Argatroban, Fondaparinux, IVIG – Choosing the Right Anticoagulant in a Patient with Severe aHIT and Stroke
blogs.description: Clinicians face a tough balance between preventing further clots and avoiding bleeding in the setting of an aHIT‑induced stroke. This post outlines the pharmacologic advantages of starting with argatroban in the ICU, the rationale for switching to fondaparinux once stable, and the evidence (and limits) for high‑dose intravenous immunoglobulin in reversing severe thrombocytopenia.

blogs.title: Ten Things to Think About When a Cardiac Bypass Patient’s Platelets Plummet
blogs.description: Early postoperative thrombocytopenia after CPB presents a diagnostic labyrinth. Here we break down ten non‑overlapping causes—from critical‑illness thrombocytopenia and infection to TTP and drug‑induced immune reactions—and provide a step‑by‑step guide to prioritizing tests, such that HIT can be ruled in or out swiftly.

blogs.title: From ICU to Home: Safely Resuming DOAC Therapy After a Hall‑Mark Case of aHIT
blogs.description: Once platelet counts recover and hypercoagulability abates, the transition back to long‑term oral anticoagulation must be planned carefully. This post reviews antithrombin assessment before fondaparinux, the safety of re‑initiating apixaban after aHIT remission, and practical monitoring strategies to guard against recurrence during the outpatient phase.
